subjects.displayTitle: Divine nearness and transcendence: finding signs without enclosing the mystery
subjects.introduction: Only the heedless are ever alone, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says; a traveller in a waterless desert who remembers God has company. Bahá’u’lláh goes further: God is nearer to a speck at the bottom of the seventh sea than it is to itself. Yet the same voices insist that the divine Essence lies beyond every image, that whatever a mind pictures as God is a creature of that mind, and that whoever presumes to describe Him has only stirred up dust. The sun never leaves the sky to enter the mirror, but the mirror is full of its light; a sign of God is deposited in every atom, and the person who looks inward finds one there too. Nearness, then, is met in the Manifestations of God, the mirrors in which the unapproachable becomes a face to turn toward. The Qur’an names God the Outward and the Inward in a single breath [1]. From here the way leads into the unknowability of God, the divine attributes within all things, and the realms of being that no lower order can comprehend.
subjects.arc: Begin with the experience of presence, explore signs and the limits of comprehension, then distinguish revelation, emanation, and the divine Essence before returning to prayer.

order.why: Hear the poem’s hidden and visible presence.
shortened: If Thou wishest me to live,
Through me blow Thy holy breath.
The touch of Jesus Thou wilt give
To me, who've lain an age in death.
Thou, both End and Origin,
Thou without and Thou within--
From every eye Thou hidest well,
And yet in every eye dost dwell.

order.why: Open with divine companionship even in a barren desert.
shortened: Only one who is heedless of God is alone. But if one is mindful of God, even if they are in a vast waterless and barren desert, they are not alone - God is with them.

order.why: Let the contrast between a speck and the sea sharpen the paradox of nearness.
Read the Bab’s paired language of concealment and manifestation.
Explore manifestation in all things beside transcendence above them.
Retain the brief assurance of presence wherever one may be.
Consider the encompassing of every world.
Read the particle’s radiance as a sign rather than a portion of the sun.
shortened: O my brother! The similitude of God is like the sun, and the similitude of creation is like objects. In every particle there is a radiance and brilliance from the sun. Likewise, in every mystery there is a secret, and in every horizon there is a light from that peerless Beloved and unique Essence.

order.why: Turn the sign within oneself toward humility about comprehension.
shortened: And when thou observest thine own powerlessness and limitation in attaining to the knowledge of the sign that exists within thyself, thou wilt surely behold with the eye of inner and outer vision thine own impotence and that of all created things in knowing the Divine Essence and the Sun of eternal glory. The acknowledgment of powerlessness in this station, when based on insight, is the utmost limit of the knowledge of the servant and the highest attainment of the worshippers.

order.why: Consider desire as an iron lantern that conceals the heart’s effulgence.
shortened: 47 Indeed, the references that have been made to the degrees of mystic knowledge pertain to the knowledge of the effulgences of that Sun of Truth as it becometh reflected in various mirrors. And the effulgence of that light is present within the hearts, yet it is hidden beneath the veils of selfish desires and earthly attachments, even as a candle within a lantern of iron, and only when the cover is lifted doth the light of the candle shine out.

order.why: Distinguish nearness to the Manifestation from a spatial account of the divine Essence.
Read the Manifestations as the accessible source of divine guidance.
shortened: O Salman! The door of the knowledge of the Ancient Being hath ever been, and will continue forever to be, closed in the face of men. No man’s understanding shall ever gain access unto His holy court. As a token of His mercy, however, and as a proof of His loving-kindness, He hath manifested unto men the Daystars of His divine guidance, the Symbols of His divine unity, and hath ordained the knowledge of these sanctified Beings to be identical with the knowledge of His own Self. Whoso recognizeth them hath recognized God.

order.why: Explore specific outpouring and the nonphysical meaning of nearness.
shortened: To every discerning and illumined heart it is evident that God, the unknowable Essence, the divine Being, is immensely exalted beyond every human attribute, such as corporeal existence, ascent and descent, egress and regress.
No tie of direct intercourse can possibly bind Him to His creatures. He standeth exalted beyond and above all separation and union, all proximity and remoteness.

order.why: Keep the reported desert traveler’s search for water as a concrete image of mediation.
shortened: Many who wrote or visited 'Abdu'l-Baha would ask this question: God being omnipresent, why would it not be enough to concentrate on His presence in the natural world, rather than to believe in a man, a Prophet, claiming to be the intermediary between man and God?

When Khan was in the Holy Land, 'Abdu'l-Baha made this reply to an American inquirer: There was once an Arab traveler who had lost his way in the desert. He was dying of thirst and, humbly, he begged God for water. Suddenly on the far horizon he saw an oasis with waving trees, and he knew that there could be no trees and greenery unless water was present too. When he had somehow dragged himself across the sands and reached the oasis, how did he go about quenching his thirst? Was his conviction enough for him, that growing things meant water? Or did he search avidly for a source, a crack in a rock or an opening in the earth where water could get through and he could drink and live?

order.why: Read the question about God’s connection with the Manifestations alongside the distinction between encompassing and encompassed.
shortened: Question: What is the reality of the Divinity and its connection to the Daysprings of Lordly splendour and the Dawning-Places of the light of the All-Merciful?
Answer: Know that the reality of the Divinity and the nature of the divine Essence is ineffable sanctity and absolute holiness, that is, it is exalted above and sanctified beyond every praise.

For the divine Essence is an all-encompassing reality, and all created things are encompassed. The all-encompassing must assuredly be greater than that which is encompassed, and thus the latter can in no wise discover the former or comprehend its reality. No matter how far human minds may advance, even attaining the highest degree of human comprehension, the uttermost limit of this comprehension is to behold the signs and attributes of God in the world of creation and not in the realm of Divinity.

order.why: Distinguish the unity of the Manifestations from an incarnation of the Essence.
shortened: The reality of Divinity is sanctified above this degree of knowing and realization. It has ever been hidden and secluded in its own holiness and sanctity above our comprehending. Although it transcends our realization, its lights, bestowals, traces and virtues have become manifest in the realities of the Prophets, even as the sun becomes resplendent in various mirrors. These holy realities are as reflectors, and the reality of Divinity is as the sun, which, although it is reflected from the mirrors, and its virtues and perfections become resplendent therein, does not stoop from its own station of majesty and glory and seek abode in the mirrors; it remains in its heaven of sanctity.

order.why: Explore what the mirror may mean by being the sun and not being the sun.
shortened: In that polished surface, the Sun with all Its majesty standeth clearly revealed. Thus, should the mirrored Sun proclaim, 'I am the Sun!' this is but truth; and should It cry, 'I am not the Sun!' this is the truth as well. And although the Day-Star, with all Its glory, Its beauty, Its perfections, be clearly visible in that mirror without stain, still It hath not come down from Its own lofty station in the realms above, It hath not made Its way into the mirror; rather doth It continue to abide, as It will forever, in the supernal heights of Its own holiness.

order.why: Read the warning about imagined divinity beside turning toward the Manifestation.
shortened: We have no recourse but to turn in all matters toward that known Center, the Promised Manifestation, and the Witnessed Dawning-Place. Otherwise, we would worship an imaginary reality conceived in minds, a rejected creation, a mere fancy rather than conscious awareness in the human world - and this would be worse than idol worship, for idols at least have existence in the world of being.

order.why: Consider the fire and its faces within the Bab’s account of revelation.
Read the many names and the indivisible point without inferring a descent of Essence.
shortened: And that essence of Primal Oneness, in that most great station in which it is said:  "There was God and there was naught else besides Him", is called by the names:  the Hidden Treasure, the Hidden Ipseity [Huwiyyat], the Absolute Unity, Pure Essence [dhat], Absolute Non-specificity, the Hidden of the Hidden, the Primal Mystery, the Absolute Unknown, the Indescribable One, the Undiscoverable One and other Names.

Therefore observe that although all letters and words appear from the point and all numbers from the unitary concept, neither does the primal point descend from its high station nor does the unitary concept come down from its abode of sanctity.

order.why: Consider names as known through God while the Essence remains beyond proof by likeness.
Explains divine reflection in a mirror while preserving the Sun’s transcendence.
Hear nearness and incomprehensibility together in the Bab’s words.
Retain the affirmation of hiddenness, nearness, and command.
Consider the divine independence from peers and comparisons.
Read the explicit distinction between Essence and manifestation.
shortened: Know thou that God - exalted and glorified be He - doth in no wise manifest His inmost Essence and Reality. From time immemorial He hath been veiled in the eternity of His Essence and concealed in the infinitude of His own Being.
Immeasurably exalted is God above that which they conceive in their hearts, and immensely glorified is He beyond that which they attribute to Him.

order.why: Hear the account of unity that leaves the Essence unfathomed.
shortened: Who is it that can claim to have attained the heights of His exalted Essence, and what mind can measure the depths of His unfathomable mystery?

From time immemorial He hath been veiled in the ineffable sanctity of His exalted Self, and will everlastingly continue to be wrapt in the impenetrable mystery of His unknowable Essence. Every attempt to attain to an understanding of His inaccessible Reality hath ended in complete bewilderment, and every effort to approach His exalted Self and envisage His Essence hath resulted in hopelessness and failure.

order.why: Distinguish names from the reality they cannot encompass.
shortened: And in one station, all that hath been or will be mentioned returneth unto the First Mention, for the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, is an impenetrable Mystery that cannot be comprehended. In this station, He was and ever shall be sanctified beyond all mentions and names, and exalted above the understanding of all created things. The way is barred and the quest forbidden.

order.why: Read knowledge of all things beside divine exaltation.
shortened: Were anyone to meditate upon this blessed and transcendent Revelation and to ponder the verses that have been sent down, he would readily bear witness that the one true God is immeasurably exalted above His creatures, and that the knowledge of all things hath ever been and shall ever remain with Him.

order.why: Consider how observed attributes support acknowledgment without providing exhaustive comprehension.
shortened: There is no doubt that these infinite beings and the association of these diverse elements arranged in countless forms must have proceeded from a Reality that could in no wise be bereft of will or understanding. This is clear and proven to the mind and no one can deny it. It is not meant, however, that that Universal Reality or the attributes thereof have been comprehended. Neither its Essence nor its true attributes hath any one comprehended.

As it hath previously been mentioned, these attributes and perfections that we recount of the Divine Essence, these we have derived from the existence and observation of beings, and it is not that we have comprehended the essence and perfection of God.

order.why: Read the limits of knowing essences even among created things.
shortened: As our knowledge of things, even of created and limited ones, is of their attributes and not of their essence, how then can it be possible to understand in its essence the unbounded Reality of the Divinity? For the inner essence of a thing can never be known, only its attributes. For example, the inner reality of the sun is unknown, but it is understood through its attributes, which are heat and light. The inner essence of man is unknown and unfathomed, but it is known and characterized by its attributes.

order.why: Examine the mind’s relation to the deity it imagines.
shortened: Consider then, how all the peoples of the world are bowing the knee to a fancy of their own contriving, how they have created a creator within their own minds, and they call it the Fashioner of all that is -- whereas in truth it is but an illusion. Thus are the people worshipping only an error of perception.
But that Essence of Essences, that Invisible of Invisibles, is sanctified above all human speculation, and never to be overtaken by the mind of man.

order.why: Consider the public address’s argument about finite concepts and the unlimited.
shortened: Therefore, the reality of Divinity in its identity is beyond the range of human intellection because the human mind, the human intellect, the human thought are limited, whereas the reality of Divinity is unlimited. How can the limited grasp the unlimited and transcend it? Impossible. The unlimited always comprehends the limited. The limited can never comprehend, surround nor take in the unlimited. Therefore, every concept of Divinity which has come within the intellection of a human being is finite, or limited, and is a pure product of imagination, whereas the reality of Divinity is holy and sacred above and beyond all such concepts.

order.why: Read the related distinction between phenomenal thought and divine reality.
shortened: It is a self-evident fact that phenomenal existence can never grasp nor comprehend the ancient and essential Reality. Utter weakness cannot understand absolute strength. When we view the world of creation, we discover differences in degree which make it impossible for the lower to comprehend the higher.

order.why: Keep the argument about finite knowledge in its reported setting.
shortened: The realm of Divinity is an indivisible oneness, wholly sanctified above human comprehension; for intellectual knowledge of creation is finite, whereas comprehension of Divinity is infinite.

order.why: Explore the relation of container, contained, and mirror in the Paris account.
shortened: God contains all: He cannot be contained. That which contains is superior to that which is contained.

The sun does not leave his place in the heavens and descend into the mirror, for the actions of ascent and descent, coming and going, do not belong to the Infinite, they are the methods of finite beings.

order.why: Use the craftsman and painting to question likeness as identity.
shortened: He is indeed a true believer in the unity of God who, in this Day, will regard Him as One immeasurably exalted above all the comparisons and likenesses with which men have compared Him. He hath erred grievously who hath mistaken these comparisons and likenesses for God Himself. Consider the relation between the craftsman and his handiwork, between the painter and his painting.

order.why: Read the denial of embodiment beside unity of Essence and attributes.
shortened: He, in truth, hath, throughout eternity, been one in His Essence, one in His attributes, one in His works.

The birds of men's hearts, however high they soar, can never hope to attain the heights of His unknowable Essence. It is He Who hath called into being the whole of creation, Who hath caused every created thing to spring forth at His behest. Shall, then, the thing that was born by virtue of the word which His Pen hath revealed, and which the finger of His Will hath directed, be regarded as partner with Him, or an embodiment of His Self? Far be it from His glory that human pen or tongue should hint at His mystery, or that human heart conceive His Essence.

order.why: Keep the question about the Trinity with the answer’s account of indivisible divinity.
shortened: Question: What is the meaning of the Trinity and of its three Persons?

Answer: The reality of the Divinity is sanctified and exalted beyond the comprehension of all created things, can in no wise be imagined by mortal mind and understanding, and transcends all human conception. That reality admits of no division, for division and multiplicity are among the characteristics of created and hence contingent things, and not accidents impinging upon the Necessary Being.
All that is mentioned regarding the manifestation and revelation of God pertains to the effulgence of His light and not to a descent into the degrees of existence.

order.why: Hear the concise rejection of incarnation of the Essence.
shortened: Say:

Know thou of a certainty that the Unseen can in no wise incarnate His Essence and reveal it unto men. He is, and hath ever been, immensely exalted beyond all that can either be recounted or perceived.

order.why: Read the reported mirror image beside the rejection of God as a body in a vessel.
Consider the reported sun’s loss of identity if divided among objects.
Read the reported impossibility of the infinite descending into the finite.
shortened: The Divine Reality is Unthinkable, Limitless, Eternal, Immortal and Invisible.
The world of creation is bound by natural law, finite and mortal.
The Infinite Reality cannot be said to ascend or descend. It is beyond the understanding of man, and cannot be described in terms which apply to the phenomenal sphere of the created world.

order.why: Examine the three-realm account and its specific critique of the sea-and-waves analogy.
shortened: In summary, the Sufis speak only of God and creation, and believe that God has resolved Himself into, and manifested Himself through, the infinite forms of His creation, even as the sea which appears in the infinite forms of its waves. These originated and imperfect waves are identical to the pre-existent Sea, which is the sum of all the divine perfections. The Prophets, however, hold that there are the world of God, the world of the Kingdom, and the world of creation: three things.

In brief, superior realities do not descend or abase themselves to the degree of inferior realities. How, then, could the universal Reality of God, which transcends all descriptions and attributes, resolve itself, notwithstanding its absolute sanctity and holiness, into the forms and realities of the contingent world, which are the very source of imperfections? This is pure fantasy and untenable conjecture.

order.why: Distinguish the Primal Will from the Essence when reading that analogy.
shortened: The truth, however, is that the reality of that sanctified Essence can in no wise descend into the realm of creation. For Him there is no egress or regress, no descent or dissolution, no composition or commingling; only infinite transcendence. He is even as the sun whose rays shine upon all earthly beings. All things are invigorated and made visible by Him, and reflect His light, whilst He remaineth, in the heights of holiness, exalted above and sanctified beyond all conditions, determinations, and distinctions, even beyond the very comprehension of His creatures. Rather is it the Primal Will, which consisteth of the radiance and bounties of that Sun, that causeth the manifestation, appearance, and visibility of all beings.

order.why: Consider the speaker remaining unchanged while speech emanates.
shortened: For the speaker remains in an absolute state of ability and power as the discourse emanates from him, even as the action emanates from its author. The true Speaker, the divine Essence, ever remains in the same condition and experiences no change or alteration, no transformation or vicissitude. It has neither beginning nor end.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast between imparting attributes and transferring substance.
shortened: Just as the sun does not communicate anything of its substance or essence to the earth, so also God does not give the world anything of His Godhood. As the sun only gives its attributes (light, warmth and power) to the earth, so also God lets His attributes shed their rays upon the world. Like the word comes forth from the speaker, the writing from the writer, the work from the creator, so the material (the thing), the spiritual (the human being), and the superspiritual (the Prophet) issues forth from and shines out of God. God works in His emanation dynamically (dispensing power).

order.why: Read absolute independence and the intermediary in the reported conversation.
Attribute the historical account of philosophers and waves to this report.
Read the report’s critique of dispersed divinity and its explanation of self-existence.
shortened: Some of the philosophers believe that God is the Supreme Reality and that every human being has a spark of this divine reality within him; that He Himself is in a state of utmost power and that all things manifest Him according to their different capacities. Therefore they hold that the Supreme Being is dispersed into infinite forms. This is the position of Plato.

We refer to Him as Self-Existent because we need to make use of a term but we do not mean that that Being can be contained within our comprehension. What is intended is the Reality from Whom all things emanate, the Reality through Whom all things exist.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s critique of philosophical unity and connection in its theological voice.
shortened: Those who claim the unity of existence are polytheists, by the testimony of existence itself, for the unity they affirm is contingent upon the existence of two, else from what station would come the negation of two and affirmation of unity? Likewise those who consider the Essence of Truth to be the cause of contingent existence.

Those who believe in causation are infidels. For causation is contingent upon the connection between cause and effect, and connection is contingent upon the existence of duality. Both stations are utterly false. Rather, the True Reality is the Essence of Truth.

order.why: Return to the reported invitation to notice signs throughout the world.
shortened: Do we not see the signs and traces of God - the Unknowable, primal Cause - scattered all about us?

order.why: Consider spiritual perfection and knowledge that still do not comprehend the Essence.
shortened: It is given to man to obtain knowledge, to attain to great spiritual perfection, to discover hidden truths and to manifest even the attributes of God; but still man cannot comprehend the Essence of God.

order.why: Read the reported sunlight analogy while retaining the source’s wording.
Consider presence without confinement to a place.
Preserve the Ocean and Gulf fragment without supplying its missing context.
Connect humility with the limits of power, learning, and wealth.
Consider the inability to fathom even divine grace.
shortened: No man can ever claim to have comprehended the nature of the hidden and manifold grace of God; none can fathom His all-embracing mercy.

order.why: Hear the acknowledgment of perplexity among thinkers.
shortened: The minds of the profoundest thinkers are sore perplexed as they contemplate the ocean of Thy knowledge, and the heaven of Thy wisdom, and the Luminary of Thy grace.

order.why: Read the limits of language through the images of book, water, and fire.
Consider praise that acknowledges its own inadequacy.
shortened: Know thou that the Divine Essence, which is called the Invisible of the Invisibles, never to be described, beyond the reach of mind -- is sanctified above any mention, any definition or hint or allusion, any acclamation or praise. In the sense that It is that It is, the intellect can never grasp It, and the soul seeking knowledge of It is but a wanderer in the desert, and far astray.

order.why: Read the prayer’s acknowledgment of the limits of knowledge.
shortened: In the sanctity of Thine own being hast Thou ever been exalted above the understanding of the learned among the Company on high, and forever wilt Thou remain enwrapped within the holiness of Thine own reality, unreached by the knowledge of those dwellers in Thine exalted Kingdom who glorify Thy Name.

order.why: Keep the prayer’s sense of inadequacy and its preserved omission.
Hear the petition that recognizes the finite character of praise.
shortened: How can I make mention of Thee, assured as I am that no tongue, however deep its wisdom, can befittingly magnify Thy name, nor can the bird of the human heart, however great its longing, ever hope to ascend into the heaven of Thy majesty and knowledge.
Exalted, immeasurably exalted, art Thou above the strivings of mortal man to unravel Thy mystery, to describe Thy glory, or to even hint at the nature of Thine Essence.

order.why: Consider the renewal of creatures as their praise of oneness.
shortened: All the phenomena are in the process of reformation and regeneration and all the creatures are chanting the verses of oneness with their tongues of consciousness and reality.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the brief prayer of supplication.
Read the supplied interpretation distinguishing the Manifestation’s divinity from incarnation of the Essence.
shortened: The human temple that has been made the vehicle of so overpowering a Revelation must, if we be faithful to the tenets of our Faith, ever remain entirely distinguished from that 'innermost Spirit of Spirits' and 'eternal Essence of Essences' - that invisible yet rational God Who, however much we extol the divinity of His Manifestations on earth, can in no wise incarnate His infinite, His unknowable, His incorruptible and all-embracing Reality in the concrete and limited frame of a mortal being.

order.why: Distinguish personal consciousness and purpose from an anthropomorphic definition.
Retain the supplied summary of the Iqan and its terminal omission.
Keep the Bab’s supplied provisional wording and its account of inaccessible Essence.
Read the supplied provisional statement of transcendence.
Consider the supplied provisional language of the Divine Spirit without merging distinct metaphysical terms.
Read the supplied account of the Prophets as mediators.
Keep the supplied Table Talks account of imagined divinity as a distinct rendering.
shortened: Now all people worship an imagination, for they have created a God in the realm of imagination and him they worship. If you ask a soul, when he is praying, who art thou worshiping? He will say, God. Which God? The God of my conception. When, in truth, what he imagines is not God. Hence, all people are worshippers of imaginations and ideals. Consequently, there is no pathway or escape for man except the Holy Manifestations, for, as we said the Essence of Divinity is pure, is holy and cannot be brought into the world of ideas. That which can be brought to ideation are the Holy and Divine Manifestations.

order.why: Read the supplied prayer’s rejection of inadequate comparisons, retaining its citation.
shortened: Any comparison is a verity emanating from the thoughts of Thy creatures. Thou art immeasurably exalted above all these and Thou art independent of that which the highest and purest minds among the distinguished of Thy chosen ones hope to attain in the apex of glory and majesty.

Thou hast, therefore, fashioned a luminous Being and an effulgent Truth, and Thou hast referred the world of creation to It and hast summoned all beings to bow down before It and hast bidden them to arrive and enter Its court. All else is verily trivial vain imaginings and hollow images. PA01513, in Makatib 1:220 and

order.why: Compare the Hermetic passage’s language of embodiment with the distinctions made earlier.
shortened: Such is He who is too great to be named God. He is hidden, yet most manifest. He is apprehensible by thought alone, yet we can see Him with our eyes. He is bodiless, and yet has many bodies, or rather, is embodied in all bodies. There is nothing that He is not; for all things that exist are even He. For this reason all names are names of Him, because all things come from Him, their one Father; and for this reason He has no name, because He is the Father of all.

order.why: Hear the supplied New Testament image of unapproachable light.
Keep the Buddhist account of the unconditioned within its own vocabulary and purpose.
Read Chittick’s modern account as a secondary interpretation rather than primary revelation.
End with the supplied poem’s paradox of intimate nearness and experienced distance.

questions: How does the opening assurance of companionship change the way you read declarations that God cannot be comprehended?
What do sunlight, mirrors, speech, and the desert traveler each reveal—and leave unexplained—about divine presence?
How do these passages distinguish the divine Essence, its signs, and the Manifestations of God?
What questions arise when Qur’an 57:3 places outward and inward together as divine names?
Where do the supplied Hermetic and Buddhist passages resemble the compilation’s language, and where do their purposes or claims differ?
How might acknowledging the limits of one’s image of God influence prayer, humility, and attention to other people?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 57:3 · Outward and inward
references.note: Read Pickthall’s translation alongside the parallel translations of the paired divine names. Compare their conjunction of outward and inward with the compilation’s distinction between divine signs and an incomprehensible Essence. Consider how a name may orient attention without enclosing the reality it names.

subjects.displayTitle: Loving one’s enemies: changing the response to injury
subjects.introduction: When relatives of the martyred were called to testify against the killers, some stayed silent, withdrew their claims, and rose instead to intercede. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá names this, with refraining from retaliation, as one of two mighty deeds, and it sets the measure for everything that follows. Loving an enemy here means more than holding back anger. It asks for a change of sight, so that the stranger is seen as kin and every creature as a sign of God, and then for a change of hand: milk and honey offered in return for darts, a balm for the wound one has been given, a greeting in answer to a curse. The same counsel keeps its judgment: one may welcome an enemy to the house with every courtesy but must not admit a thief, and kindness stops short of consenting to harm. Jesus’ command to love one’s enemies, with the sun and rain that fall on the just and the unjust, stands as the nearest comparison [1]. The way leads on through forgiveness, prayer for opponents, the golden rule, and the slow work of a virtuous life.
subjects.arc: Open with intercession for persecutors, explore universal regard and discernment, then follow the movement from speech and practical help to historical witness and prayer.

order.why: Explore the perception of every person as a sign of God and a member of the family.
shortened: For each of the creatures is a sign of God, and it was by the grace of the Lord and His power that each did step into the world; therefore they are not strangers, but in the family; not aliens, but friends, and to be treated as such.

If others hurl their darts against you, offer them milk and honey in return; if they poison your lives, sweeten their souls; if they injure you, teach them how to be comforted; if they inflict a wound upon you, be a balm to their sores; if they sting you, hold to their lips a refreshing cup.

order.why: Open with the concrete act of interceding for enemies before the authorities.
shortened: Two mighty deeds were manifested by the friends in that land: first, refraining from retaliation against the oppressors, and second, interceding with the authorities on behalf of their enemies.

order.why: Read the related account of relatives withdrawing their claims and interceding.
Read universal love together with rectitude, justice, and truthfulness.
shortened: It is incumbent upon everyone to show the utmost love, rectitude of conduct, straightforwardness and sincere kindliness unto all the peoples and kindreds of the world, be they friends or strangers. So intense must be the spirit of love and loving kindness, that the stranger may find himself a friend, the enemy a true brother, no difference whatsoever existing between them.

Should other peoples and nations be unfaithful to you show your fidelity unto them, should they be unjust toward you show justice towards them, should they keep aloof from you attract them to yourselves, should they show their enmity be friendly towards them, should they poison your lives, sweeten their souls, should they inflict a wound upon you, be a salve to their sores.

order.why: Keep the explicit distinction between kindness and allowing a thief or wolf into a place of trust.
shortened: One may allow an enemy into one's house and show them the utmost consideration and respect, but it is not permissible to let a thief into the house, nor is it permissible to let a traitor into the house, nor is it permissible to let a wolf into the flock.
But you should show the utmost kindness to enemies - that is, ignorant enemies, not treacherous thieving enemies.

order.why: Consider the stated limit of showing consideration to a degree that causes no harm.
Examine the invitation to draw no lines of prejudice.
shortened: Let them see no one as their enemy, or as wishing them ill, but think of all humankind as their friends; regarding the alien as an intimate, the stranger as a companion, staying free of prejudice, drawing no lines.

order.why: Consider the image of other people as members of one’s own body.
shortened: Now we must not consider nor recognize these mirrors, which are deprived of every gift, as strangers and foreigners; neither should we speak of or know them as enemies or savages; nay, rather, must we recognize them as the members of our body, showing them love and affection; not as strangers but as associates; not as foreigners but as friends.

order.why: Read tenderness across generations and toward those who persecute.
Hear the injunction to treat all as close kin.
Read the source’s appeal to humanity’s dignity and mercy.
shortened: That is, they must treat enemies in a manner worthy of friends and deal with oppressors in a way befitting faithful companions. They must not look upon the sins, shortcomings, enmity, injustice and oppression of their foes, but rather consider that the Blessed Beauty hath referred to humanity as His most glorious servants, hath declared that mankind is preceded by mercy, and hath commanded all to show love, fellowship, unity, wisdom, faithfulness and kindness to the entire human race without any restrictions.

order.why: Notice the explanation of extraordinary love as treating others with the conduct due to friends.
shortened: One amongst His Teachings is this, that love and good faith must so dominate the human heart that men will regard the stranger as a familiar friend, the malefactor as one of their own, the alien even as a loved one, the enemy as a companion dear and close. Who killeth them, him will they call a bestower of life; who turneth away from them, him will they regard as turning towards them; who denieth their message, him will they consider as one acknowledging its truth. The meaning is that they must treat all humankind even as they treat their sympathizers, their fellow-believers, their loved ones and familiar friends.

order.why: Read the same standard through virtuous deeds.
Connect friendship with followers of every religion to everyday virtue.
shortened: He exhorted us instead to "consort with the followers of all religions in a spirit of friendliness and fellowship". He ordained that we be loving friends and well-wishers of all peoples and religions, and enjoined upon us to demonstrate the highest virtues in our dealings with the kindreds of the earth. He even regarded enemies as friends, and considered strangers as comrades and intimate companions.

order.why: Consider mercy extended across wealth, kinship, and religious difference.
Read friendship offered to outsiders and opponents.
Hear the brief invitation to regard strangers as familiar.
shortened: Rather, be well-wishers to ill-wishers and become heart and soul friends to enemies. Consider strangers as familiar and others as friends.

order.why: Consider the joyful rather than reluctant character of kindness.
shortened: That is, consider the bitter enemy as a loving friend, and know the fierce opponent as an intimate companion, so that you may show them love and kindness with the utmost joy and fragrance.

order.why: Explore the change of perception described through nearness and sight.
shortened: Then shalt thou see thine enemies as thy friends. Then shalt thou perceive strangers as acquaintances and distant ones as close ones. Thou shalt understand the blind may be those who truly see.

order.why: Read justice and love as enduring light beside the shadow of oppression.
Read the Gospel comparison within The Secret of Divine Civilization.
Consider the appeal to Christian teaching as a standard for conduct.
shortened: In the glorious Gospel it is said: "Love your enemies and be well-wishers to those who wish you ill; respond to oppression and cruelty with love and faithfulness." Now, if there be fairness, it will be observed that this is truly the way and conduct of these wanderers and the character of these free souls.

order.why: Hear the public address’s question about persecution and the teaching of Christ.
Keep the reported Gospel citation in its service-centered setting.
shortened: He came into this world to minister and not to be ministered unto. His greatest commandment was, "But I say unto you, love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; that ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven; for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

order.why: Attribute the historical contrast between Mosaic and Christian law to this reported address.
Read the reported possibility of attaining love for persecutors.
shortened: We must love all, therefore, as creatures or children of the same God, even though they are doing us harm. Christ loved his persecutors. It is possible for us to attain to that degree of love.

order.why: Hear kindness toward enemies described as following Christ.
Keep the reported question about an unpleasant personality with the answer.
shortened: How can we love another whose personality is unpleasant?
See how the enemies of Christ persecuted and crucified Him, yet He loved them all.

order.why: Read the reported grounding of love in God’s creation rather than personal attraction.
Consider affection that does not depend on personal compatibility.
shortened: But you must, for the sake of God, show consideration and love to souls because of their faith and certitude, even when there is no cause for affection between you.

order.why: Examine the public address’s distinction between tolerating and loving.
Keep the reported aim of harmony among all humanity.
Read the reported connection among forgiveness and goodwill.
Hear the reported freedom expressed through kindness to all.
Consider the reported explanation of unfamiliarity with divine love.
shortened: They must not just love their friends but should also be kind to their enemies and indeed count them as friends. Since these people have not drunk from the chalice of divine love, they know not [such sentiments].

order.why: Read the reported equal regard for friend and enemy.
Calls for the same truthful and loving treatment of enemies and friends.
Bring the demand back to one’s treatment of friends.
shortened: We are commanded to deal with the utmost love and kindness even with our enemies, how much more so with friends.

order.why: Consider its implications for close relatives.
shortened: We should show the utmost love, love from the bottom of our hearts, even to those who hate us, how much more so our close relatives

order.why: Read the hypothetical city where only a few remain hostile.
Consider the practice of not centering attention on shortcomings.
shortened: They should not look at shortcomings and should not be offended by harmful people, but rather should consider enemies as friends and ill-wishers as well-wishers, and treat them accordingly.

order.why: Read gentleness and instruction as responses to estrangement.
shortened: O friends! Take no offense at strangers and be not grieved by outsiders. They are ignorant - excuse them. They are veiled - remove their veils. Show kindness and practice good conduct. Be gentle and peaceful, and become an intimate companion to every stranger.

order.why: Consider neighborliness as something to teach by kindness.
Read the hope that hostility may change into friendship.
Keep the reported possibility of changed character without turning it into a guaranteed result.
shortened: You should conquer hatred by love. If you meet with kindness him who injures you, you may overcome his stubborn spirit. The love of God will then come to him, and he will become a changed man.

order.why: Examine the rejection of insult, humiliation, and retaliation in this particular Tablet.
Read praise, silence, and justice as alternatives to accusation.
shortened: If thou perceivest from any soul the fragrances of God, unloose thy tongue in his glorification and praise, but otherwise remain silent. Nay, should a soul find fault with thee, praise him instead; should he condemn thee, commend him in return; should he commit an iniquity, show forth justice in exchange.

order.why: Connect a greeting in response to cursing with the Tablet’s lament over war.
Keep the specific counsel concerning fellow countrymen and taunting.
shortened: But some fellow countrymen may not understand - if they taunt or act unjustly, you must do the opposite. That is, in response to cursing and condemnation, offer praise and commendation. In place of deadly poison, give honey and milk.

order.why: Read the practical sequence of considerate responses to harm and accusation.
Consider humility in response to pride and peace in response to reproach.
Read the images of assistance and blessings in response to scorn.
shortened: O friends of God! You must do the opposite and act in contrary manner: place a healing salve upon the wounds of the oppressors and become a remedy for the pain of the wrongdoers. Should they offer poison, give them honey in return; should they draw the sword, give them milk and sweetmeats; should they heap scorn, render assistance; should they pronounce a curse, seek for them divine blessings.

order.why: Consider medicine, roses, and honey as images of transformative response.
shortened: Should any come to blows with you, seek to be friends with him; should any stab you to the heart, be ye a healing salve unto his sores; should any taunt and mock at you, meet him with love. Should any heap his blame upon you, praise ye him; should he offer you a deadly poison, give him the choicest honey in exchange; and should he threaten your life, grant him a remedy that will heal him evermore. Should he be pain itself, be ye his medicine; should he be thorns, be ye his roses and sweet herbs.

order.why: Hear the related sequence of wounds and remedies.
shortened: If they draw daggers, you must offer life-giving elixir. If they give deadly poison, you must bestow pure honey. If they permit arrows and spears, you must lavish spirit and fragrance. If they inflict wounds to the heart, you must apply salve and become the remedy of heart and soul.

order.why: Read the brief paired images of injury and healing.
shortened: Become loving friends to enemies and spiritual companions to foes. If struck, show mercy. If wounded, apply a balm. If given deadly poison, give sweet honey in return.

order.why: Keep fairness and grace together in the face of oppression.
Explore the movement from war and fire toward peace and healing.
shortened: If they desire war, seek ye peace. If they bring pain, bestow treasure. If they kindle fire, cause it to be extinguished. If they inflict a sting, give honey in return. If they offer poison, mix it with nectar. If they bring pain, give healing. If they show the flame of wrath, display the light of kindness.

order.why: Retain the striking gazelle-and-wolf image in its devotional voice.
shortened: See foes as friends; see demons as angels; give to the tyrant the same great love ye show the loyal and true, and even as gazelles from the scented cities of Khata and Khutan offer up sweet musk to the ravening wolf.

order.why: Keep the shaman and snake-charmer metaphors attributed to the source.
shortened: Even if an enemy be an idol-worshipper, they should become shamans, and if an ill-wisher be a black snake, they should become loving charmers. They should not hurt any heart nor cause pain to any soul.

order.why: Read the hoped-for transformation of deceit and despair.
shortened: Let them become manifestations of bounty to their enemies and heavenly sustenance to their foes. Let them treat the oppressors with absolute fidelity, become trusted ones to the treacherous, teach truthfulness to the deceitful, transform demons into angels, become healing balm to the bloodthirsty, become centers of hope for the hopeless, and bestow abundant portions upon the deprived.

order.why: Consider sincerity toward governments and peoples alongside kindness to opponents.
shortened: Likewise, they must treat with and behave toward all the governments, nations, communities, kings and subjects with the utmost sincerity, trustworthiness, straightforwardness, love and kindness. Even they must make hopeful a bloodthirsty enemy, show sympathy with the utmost faithfulness and honor to the perfidious unjust, know the ill-wisher as the well-wisher and torment not the sinner with reproaches. Should they become the targets of a thousand arrows of persecution, they must challenge it with love and friendship and treat every one with purity of purpose and kindness.

order.why: Keep the specific counsel about service and Iran within its historical setting.
shortened: They must show kindness to all people, even to enemies and ill-wishers, serve the throne faithfully, and obey the authorities with perfect good will, that they may become the cause of the ancient glory of that realm and the means of fame and renown for the people of Iran.

order.why: Read service to opponents as part of service to humanity.
Hear the response to a letter reporting love and service to enemies.
shortened: And from these words written in the letter - that they love their enemies, serve those who detest them, and seek mercy for all - how sweet and delightful these words were to this yearning one!

order.why: Consider kindness and assistance to the extent possible.
Keep the reported nondiscriminatory relief of needs central to practical service.
Read the reported practical invitation to welcome visitors; retain its historical cultural generalization.
Extend the circle of hospitality to animals and birds.
shortened: Even show hospitality to wild beasts and birds, and show kindness to enemies and ill-wishers.

order.why: Hear the concise invitation to care for all as much as possible.
shortened: As much as you can, be kind and caring to all people, even enemies, and associate with them. Become a balm for souls and healing for aching hearts.

order.why: Connect care for the afflicted with the removal of selfish prejudice.
Read reconciliation and prayer as responses to conflict.
shortened: Resist their fighting with peace and reconciliation, their blows with kindness and perfection and their blame with joy and tranquillity. Do beseech God to direct them to the Path of Salvation and breathe into them the Spirit of Life.

order.why: Consider pardon grounded in the source’s understanding of ignorance.
shortened: Thou must show the utmost love and kindness towards the heedless ones and the oppressors and ask from God forgiveness and pardon for them, for they are ignorant. if they understood, they would not oppress; nay, rather would they arise (to serve the Cause) with faithfulness."

order.why: Read mercy that astonishes observers and responds to evil with good.
shortened: However, the loved ones of God must become well-wishers to those oppressors and seek pardon and forgiveness for them from God, and deal with them in such a way that everyone becomes astonished at their kindness.
One must show mercy to such souls and respond to evil with good.

order.why: Keep the source’s description of opponents as overcome by their own selves.
Read the rejection of revenge alongside cherishing enemies.
Consider patience and composure amid hostile speech.
shortened: O friends! You must behave with the utmost forbearance and tranquility, and show patience in all matters. You must praise and extol those who speak ill of you, and wish well for those who wish you ill. Be kind to those who are bloodthirsty, and deliver the savage from their savagery.

order.why: Join trust, dignity, faithfulness, and love under pressure.
Retain the concise counsel concerning denunciation and slander.
Read generosity toward slips of pen and tongue.
shortened: Strengthen thy back and renew thy flesh and associate with the hostile ones with spirituality and fragrance. Treat them with grace and kindness and overlook their slips of pen and tongue.

order.why: Consider increasing affection when others withdraw.
shortened: But the more the tormenting friends shun thee, go thou nearer to them. The more they deride and blame thee, show thou forth the greater love and affection.

order.why: Keep the source’s demanding counsel about growing bitterness and its omission.
Read the reported concern not to injure a heart even with a word.
shortened: Bear all sorrow, for yourselves and to please all hearts, even the hearts of your enemies. Be true to all the different parties or nations and act toward them with faithfulness.
Beware not to cause any sorrow to them, not even to injure the feelings of anyone with a word. Do nothing to cause any sorrow within any heart.

order.why: Distinguish gentleness toward others from abandoning one’s faith.
shortened: If they oppose you be gentle with them, if they contradict be firm in your faith, if they desert you and flee from before you, seek them out and treat them kindly. Do harm to nobody; pray for all; try to make your light shine in the world and let your banner fly high in the Heavens.

order.why: Hear the reported practical vow of peace and absence of resentment.
Keep the report’s challenging whip metaphor in its mutual-encouragement setting.
shortened: Now we, as offenders against the opinions our friends and enemies, must assist each other to become impervious to their criticism, unconscious of attack, welcoming their whips. You must beat me and I will beat you with the whips of love. The more we beat each other the more capable of withstanding we will become. When the enemies find they are increasing our love, enkindlement and service in the pathway of Baha'u'llah, they will wonder and say, "How is this? Our words have no effect upon them except to make them love us more and give thanks to God for our scourging."

order.why: Read the reported personal exchange about love and hatred.
Consider the reported difference between reading a teaching and responding when provoked.
shortened: "'What would you do,' I asked 'if I were to suddenly turn and strike you?' He instantly flared with indignation and strode angrily about the room.
"After a little I went over and took his arm, saying, 'But you must return good for evil. Whether I honoured you or despised you, you should follow the teachings; now you merely read them.

order.why: Keep the reported hospitality toward someone who acted treacherously as a distinct personal account.
Read the Ishqabad account as a specific historical witness to intercession.
shortened: They even consider enemies as friends and treat ill-wishers as well-wishers. No tricks, no deception, no dissimulation and no schemes - under the sword they raise the cry of "Ya Baha'ul-Abha" and intercede on behalf of their own killer, as happened in Ishqabad where seven people killed and martyred a respected person who was infinitely kind to all and had rendered notable services to all Iranians and was renowned throughout the world for human perfections.

order.why: Retain the testimony about martyrdom and its extraordinary gesture toward a killer.
shortened: But some, at the moment of being struck by sword and dagger from the oppressor's hand, would cry out "Lord forgive them for they know not what they do," while another would take candy from his pocket and give it to his killer saying "With a sweet mouth spill this crimson blood, that your palate may become like mine - sugar-sweet."

order.why: Keep the parallel reported rock-candy episode in its historical setting.
shortened: These martyrs held in their hands rock candy for the express purpose of offering it to the executioner to whom they said: 'Have a sweet taste before offering us the cup of sacrifice.' Thus did they show such kindness to those who hatefully discharged their arrows at them, and used their revolvers and swords against them.

order.why: Attribute the account of Mary’s intercession to the reported narrative.
Keep the source’s harsh characterization of opponents separate from the editor’s voice.
shortened: As much as they can, they consider both friend and stranger as one companion, and regard the enemy as a trusted friend - meaning they imagine no enemies and harbor no ill will.

Their purpose is to cut off the root of humanity, especially you, for the foundation of this sect is bloodthirstiness while your foundation is forbearance, gentleness, meekness, and even goodwill toward every enemy, kindness toward every hostile one, love for all humanity of every religion and faith, and sincerity toward all people of every creed and nation.

order.why: Read the remembrance of Nazim through anger restrained and kindness practiced.
shortened: Verily Your servant Nazim was one who suppressed anger and forgave sins and harm, showing kindness to enemies even if they were the most bitter foes, thirsting for the fountainhead of guidance, yearning to attain the Supreme Concourse, and eagerly anticipating the appointed time until his desire was fulfilled and his destiny arrived, and he drank the cup of death and soared like a dove to the flying place of the birds of immortality.

order.why: Hear the prayer for those remembered as forgiving under oppression.
shortened: They treated the enemies with love and affection.

O Lord! Make Thou firm their feet in the Straight Way and cause them to enter in Thy Delectable Paradise! Verily they have dealt with the people of oppression with the utmost amity and forgiveness and they rejoice over their trials.

order.why: Allow the prayer to acknowledge the actual danger faced by those serving humanity.
shortened: O God, my God! Thou beholdest Thy servants who are sincere towards all humanity, even their enemies, and who, with pure hearts and sanctified breasts, serve the entire human race. They are in grave danger from the darts and arrows that rain down upon them and from the pointed spears and unsheathed swords that are drawn against them.

order.why: Read prayer for pardon alongside love and concord.
shortened: Yet we only treat with them with love, fellowship and concord and call upon God to shed His grace and mercy upon them. We pray for their pardon and forgiveness for what they have inflicted on the people of understanding.

order.why: Bring the prayerful response into a relationship with a brother.
Keep the forceful description of opponents within the prayer’s wish for their transformation.
shortened: They should pray for these heedless ones that they may be freed from the nature and disposition of savagery, ferocity, wolfishness and recklessness, and seek the path of God and follow the way of guidance. This is the attribute of the spiritual ones and this is the characteristic of the merciful ones.

order.why: Hear the direct personal intercession for those who have shown hatred.
shortened: With all humility and submission I intercede for them before Thee, even though they shot at me with arrows of hatred.

order.why: Read the short prayer embracing relatives and enemies together.
Consider the aspiration to become a letter in the book of love.
shortened: Thou hadst expressed the hope to become a letter in the book of love, to discover truth, to love enemies, and to remain steadfast in the Cause of God.

order.why: Read service without seeking a reward from those served.
shortened: Do not seek from them any reward whatever, but seek all grace and beneficence from thy Lord, and even deal with the people of great oppression in faithfulness, for as much as this is becoming of the people of Baha'.

order.why: Retain the concise commitment to goodwill and faithfulness.
shortened: Rather, in every case thou shouldst requite evil deeds with good ones, and respond to censure with praise. Thou shouldst become well-wishing toward the ill-wisher and faithful toward the oppressor.

order.why: Join care for friends with wishing prosperity for enemies.
shortened: They must render devoted service to the friends, wish prosperity for enemies, show kindness to the bad tempered, and be affectionate toward the unjust.

order.why: Turn the subject toward the hope of peace for all humanity.
shortened: As long as thou canst, wish thou the most great peace for mankind: Associate with all in perfect love and kindness; hold all dear and count all friends and familiar ones; know no enemies; imagine no strangers.

order.why: Close the linked readings with a prayer to become refuge, healing, and nourishment for others.
Read the supplied parallel rendering of love as conduct befitting friends.
Consider the supplied distinction between inward freedom from hatred and outward politeness.
shortened: Recognize your enemies as friends, and consider those who wish you evil as the wishers of good. You must not see evil as evil and then compromise with your opinion, for to treat in a smooth, kindly way one whom you consider evil or an enemy is hypocrisy, and this is not worthy or allowable. You must consider your enemies as your friends, look upon your evil-wishers as your well-wishers and treat them accordingly. Act in such a way that your heart may be free from hatred.

order.why: End with the supplied Quranic image of an enemy becoming a loyal friend.

questions: What distinguishes interceding for an enemy from simply refraining from retaliation?
How do these readings connect a change in perception with truthful and just conduct?
How might kindness coexist with the distinctions about trust, protecting a household, and avoiding harm?
What does Matthew 5:43–48 add through its images of sunlight and rain shared by all?
Which ordinary practices of speech, hospitality, or assistance could widen the circle of people you regard as neighbors?
How do the historical witnesses and closing prayers deepen—and complicate—your understanding of forgiveness?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 5:43–48 · Love beyond reciprocity
references.note: Read the King James Version of Jesus’ teaching on loving and praying for enemies. Follow the argument from the Father’s sun and rain to the question of loving only those who love us. Compare this with the compilation’s practical forms of universal regard and its particular passages on discernment.

subjects.displayTitle: Assisting God: the victory that begins within the heart
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh commands His servants to come to the aid of a God who needs nothing in heaven or on earth, and the command turns out to be a gift to the helper: it detaches him from all else and draws him near. In the Tablet to the Shah He explains that assisting God never means fighting or disputing with anyone; the only lawful sword is that of utterance, wisdom and understanding, and the first city it must conquer is the helper’s own heart. Only then may one set out toward the hearts of others. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds that outward triumphs vanish like a dewdrop while spiritual victory shines like a sun, and that even a single breath of aid is counted. The Qur’án’s account of the disciples answering Jesus’s call to become helpers of God sets this reciprocal language beside its Bahá’í explanation [1]. The journey continues into the call to action, into teaching the Cause, and into the inner struggle that the old language of armies and conquest was always describing, and it rests, finally, in prayer for victory.
subjects.arc: Begin with victory over self and divine independence, establish the meaning of assistance through wisdom and deeds, then explore courage, small contributions, enduring results, and prayer.

order.why: Read the Tablet to the Shah’s extended definition of assistance and rejection of contention and killing.
shortened: It followeth, therefore, that rendering assistance unto God, in this day, doth not and shall never consist in contending or disputing with any soul; nay rather, what is preferable in the sight of God is that the cities of men's hearts, which are ruled by the hosts of self and passion, should be subdued by the sword of utterance, of wisdom and of understanding.  Thus, whoso seeketh to assist God must, before all else, conquer, with the sword of inner meaning and explanation, the city of his own heart and guard it from the remembrance of all save God, and only then set out to subdue the cities of the hearts of others.

Such is the true meaning of rendering assistance unto God.  Sedition hath never been pleasing unto God, nor were the acts committed in the past by certain foolish ones acceptable in His sight.  Know ye that to be killed in the path of His good pleasure is better for you than to kill.

order.why: Open with the explicit statement that God’s victory is victory over self.
Ask why assistance is commanded when God is independent of it.
shortened: Be as one soul in upholding the Cause, then aid your Lord, the All-Merciful, the Most Compassionate, though He is in truth independent of the help of all in the heavens and earth, if ye be of them that are endued with insight. He commandeth His servants to render aid that they may thereby detach themselves from all else but Him and turn towards a holy and luminous direction.

order.why: Consider the parallel explanation of conquering one’s own heart through spiritual truth.
shortened: Therefore, to assist God's Cause in this day doth not and shall never mean to engage in opposition and contention or conflict with any soul. Rather, what is preferable is that the cities of men's hearts should be conquered through the sword of wisdom and of utterance, and not through the sword of iron. Thus should anyone desire to assist the Cause of God, let him first conquer the city of his own heart with the sword of spiritual truth and of expression, cleanse it from all things save God, and then turn towards the cities of others' hearts. This is the meaning of assisting God's Cause that hath dawned from the horizon of the finger of the King of Names.

order.why: Make goodly words and righteous deeds a concrete standard.
shortened: Aid ye the All-Merciful through goodly words and righteous deeds. Thus have ye been commanded in the Tablets from the presence of One All-Knowing, All-Informed.

order.why: Identifies righteous deeds and praiseworthy character as the hosts of divine assistance.
Read divine qualities rather than harshness as the means of victory.
Explore self-mastery through the specific restraints on hands, feet, eyes, and heart.
Distinguish the lasting effects of spiritual victory from passing outward results.
shortened: Victory is of two kinds: one pertains to the physical world and the other to the spiritual realm. Although both are desired and beloved, and both are accepted and yearned for, yet physical victories have no abundant results or praiseworthy effects - they are but a moment, expressed as a dewdrop. But spiritual, divine victory is a sun whose rays are eternal, whose heat is everlasting, whose zenith is pre-existent and whose waves are immortal.

order.why: Read recognition itself as a meaning of assistance.
Consider turning and arising as a victory already accepted.
shortened: Your turning to the Ka'bah of Glory and arising to promote His Cause is itself a victory, and God, exalted be His glory, hath accepted it and recorded you among the helpers in the Preserved Tablet.

order.why: Read obedience and good pleasure as the criterion of true help.
shortened: I testify that thou hast rendered victorious assistance unto thy Lord and art accounted among His helpers. By My testimony all things bear witness - this is the foundation, wert thou to be among those who know. What thou doest by His command and good-pleasure is true help in the sight of thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Explore turning to God as assistance to oneself.
Read nearness as the intended benefit of the summons to help.
shortened: Say: O servants of the All-Merciful! Aid your Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, in this Revelation which hath appeared in His Most Glorious Name, and turn not your attention to whatsoever hath been created between earth and heaven. This is better for you, did ye but know. He desireth naught for you save to draw you nigh unto a sublime station of glory.

order.why: Consider detachment from possessions as preparation for service.
Hear the call to offer assistance through one’s own self.
shortened: He loveth faithfulness, abandoneth not those who love Him, wasteth not the reward of those who seek Him, and remaineth not distant from those who draw nigh unto Him. For such a Lord must ye offer your praise and remembrance and render Him assistance through your own selves.

order.why: Read the promise of divine help beyond presently known worlds.
Consider the value assigned to a single breath of assistance.
Read the related encouragement concerning even a minute contribution.
Include both the strong and those strengthened from weakness.
shortened: Blessed is the strong one who hath arisen to serve the Cause and the weak one who hath been strengthened through the power of his Lord, the Mighty, the Bountiful.

order.why: Consider the opening of acceptance and mercy through particular people.
Keep the remembrance of a woman’s assistance and other handmaidens’ response.
Read the personal example of spending possessions for service.
Consider the testimony to those who cast aside worldly attachments.
shortened: Ye are they who cast away the world and hastened unto God, the Ancient of Days, whilst the nations were in manifest loss. Ye are they who aided God upon the earth and made manifest His sovereign power over all worlds. We bear witness unto you: through you were banners raised by the hands of bounty, and ye testified to that whereunto God Himself testified ere the creation of the heavens and the earth---that there is none other God but Him, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Hear the remembrance of one who acted after hearing and reading.
shortened: O My Most Exalted Pen! We have desired to make mention of one who has turned towards My horizon when he heard My call and arose to render Me victorious when he read My mighty Book.

order.why: Read the assurance that the reward of devoted effort may be recorded.
shortened: Be thou assured of thy Lord's favor, for He recordeth for whomsoever He willeth the reward of one who, with His leave, hath turned to Him, traversed land and sea in His love, presented himself at the door, and hearkened to the call of the Lord of the Final Return.

order.why: Consider nurture, utterance, and bringing others near together.
shortened: We have nurtured thee for My help and have cast upon thee the Word from the tongue of grandeur that thou mayest arise to make mention of Me amongst My servants and bring them nigh unto the heaven of My loving-kindness and cause them to enter My hallowed and exalted Kingdom.

order.why: Read utterance as the stated means of victory.
shortened: In these days, mention of the Truth and victory for the Truth take precedence over all deeds, and victory has been and shall be through utterance.

order.why: Hear the question concerning those who assist through wisdom and speech.
shortened: And dost thou see in the heavens any who speak My Name and arise to aid My Cause through wisdom and utterance, forsaking all else out of love for God, the Lord of all worlds?

order.why: Retain the concise counsel to aid through wisdom.
Read standards and hosts explicitly defined as wisdom, remembrance, and exposition.
Consider the hosts of exposition in the preserved source ranges.
Read wisdom, utterance, and divine good pleasure together.
shortened: God willing, you will be assisted and confirmed at all times in the remembrance of Truth and the victory of the Cause of Truth through wisdom and utterance and through what He loves and is pleased with in all matters.

order.why: Interpret the swords of hearts beside the earlier explicit explanations.
shortened: Say: O people of earth, aid God, your Lord, with the swords of your hearts, with whatsoever power ye possess in the kingdom.

order.why: Keep the personal sword image connected to the regions of hearts.
Read the spiritual battle line within its figurative religious setting.
shortened: Then you will observe how this host of the armies of life and this contingent of the forces of salvation will arrange such a spiritual battle line that the ranks and thousands of the peoples and tribes of the world will be broken one by one, and "verily Our hosts shall be victorious" will become manifest.

order.why: Consider the summons to action accompanied by promised confirmation.
shortened: If you remain steadfast and firm, know with certainty that you will be assisted by the confirmations of the Most Glorious Kingdom and will be enabled to serve the Kingdom of God, for by the power of the Word of God and the breaths of the Holy Spirit, all the mighty forces of the angels of heaven are arrayed in the highest horizon, waiting for a soul to charge forth in the arena of the Kingdom so that all may render victory and assistance.

order.why: Read the assurance of assistance from the Concourse on high.
shortened: Verily, We behold you from Our realm of glory, and shall aid whosoever will arise for the triumph of Our Cause with the hosts of the Concourse on high and a company of Our favored angels."

order.why: Hear the exhortation to steadfast people concerning heavenly hosts.
Consider strength of heart and freedom from fear as the promised qualities of helpers.
shortened: Say: God shall soon raise up a people possessed of mighty strength, and through them will He aid the Youth as He aided Him the first time. These shall not be hindered by veils nor withheld by allusions, for this is not difficult for God. Their hearts are as blocks of iron, such that nothing in the heavens or earth shall cause them fear.

order.why: Read steadfastness that astonishes minds.
shortened: Aid the Cause of your Lord with such steadfastness as will cause spirits and minds to be amazed.

order.why: Consider continual effort as the practical expression of steadfastness.
Hear the injunction to aid in all conditions.
shortened: Aid thou the Cause of thy Lord in all conditions - the hosts of earth and heaven shall not prevent Me.

order.why: Read remembrance despite the might of oppressors.
shortened: It behooveth you both to arise at all times to make mention of Me and to aid My Cause in such wise that the might of the oppressors shall not deter you.

order.why: Connect steadfastness with summoning others to service.
Consider action after hearing the call.
Hear the summons to awaken and arise.
shortened: Say: O ye that slumber, awaken at the call of God! O ye that sit still, arise to aid His Cause, the All-Subduing, the Lord of all worlds!

order.why: Read the urgency of using the opportunity of the present day.
shortened: O helpers of victory! By God, this is His Day, were ye of them that know. O ye who are endowed with power! This is the Day whereon it behoveth you to arise with your might to aid the Cause of your Lord, the Mighty, the Inaccessible. Seize ye these days and then aid your Lord, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Retain the brief direct call to arise.
Consider the duty of aid among other servants.
Read aid and remembrance together in the address to the people of guidance.
shortened: On such a Day as this, it behooveth you to aid and remember your Creator, O people of guidance!

order.why: Keep the warning about opponents within the source’s theological voice.
Read the Bab’s invocation of divine names as a distinct formulation of assistance.
Preserve the historical report of anxiety about a call to travel to Baghdad without turning it into a general instruction.
shortened: A letter from your honor arrived before this servant indicating excessive anxiety and distress. Nothing was observed therein except the mention that two persons in that land had read a writing which indicated that people should go to Baghdad to render assistance to the Truth.

order.why: Hear the testimony of proclaiming the Cause alone and unafraid.
shortened: Alone and unaided I have, by the power of Thy might, arisen to proclaim Thy Cause, unafraid of the host of my oppressors.

order.why: Keep the personal praise of faithfulness and sacrifice in its devotional setting.
Read the account of speaking before opponents as testimony to endurance.
shortened: They have arisen to promote Thy Cause and have spoken forth Thy Name before the faces of Thine enemies, despite those who denied Thy proof and Thy signs, and who committed that which caused the dwellers of Thy Kingdom and Thy Realm to lament.

order.why: Consider consolation in the midst of what has occurred.
shortened: Ye must never be saddened, for whatever has occurred has been in the path of God. Blessed are those souls who have been patient and grateful in times of tribulation.

order.why: Read hidden olive oil becoming visible light as a promise about the results of noble aims.
shortened: For ultimately the radiance of the Kingdom will overwhelm the darkness of the world of being, and the holy, exalted character of your aims will become unmistakably apparent. Nothing shall remain concealed: the olive oil, though stored within the deepest vault, shall one day burn in brightness from the lamp atop the beacon.

order.why: Consider acceptance and steadfastness as a fragrance shared with the world.
Hear the assurance of grace alongside the promised banners of victory.
Read the promise of future joy for the sincere.
shortened: Soon shall come a day wherein the standards of victory and power shall be raised in the name of thy Lord, the Chosen One, and on that day the sincere shall be in great joy.

order.why: Retain the brief declaration of enduring divine sovereignty.
shortened: Soon shall the banners of victory be upraised, and sovereignty shall remain with God, the Mighty, the All-Bestowing.

order.why: Consider the promise of assistance and relief for the oppressed.
shortened: God will soon raise up His Cause in truth and will waft the breezes of glory upon the oppressed, and the Bird of Unity will sing in the midst of heaven that this is the Day wherein God will assist His Cause.

order.why: Keep the source’s contrast between the sincere and opponents in its own theological voice.
shortened: Soon shall the sincere ones find the signs of their Lord's victory, the All-Merciful, and by them shall those who associate partners with God be shaken.

order.why: Read the allusions to Pharaoh and Nimrod within the account of oppression.
shortened: O 'Ali, O thou who gazest upon My face! The servant who is present hath laid before Me thy letter at a time when sorrows have encompassed Me from all directions by reason of what hath befallen My loved ones at the hands of the aggressive forces. O 'Ali! The idolators desired to extinguish the fire of God and put out His light. Say: Perdition betide you, O company of the lost! Did Pharaoh attain what he desired, or did Nimrod profit from what he wrought? Nay, by the Self of God Who dominateth all who are in the heavens and on earth!

order.why: Retain the forceful fire and wrath imagery without displacing the explicit definitions of assistance.
shortened: Be as a flame of fire to the wicked, or as the wrath of the Almighty against the evil ones - this behooveth thee if thou art of those who act.

order.why: Keep the prayer for defeat of claimants in its particular religious setting.
Read the reversal of imprisonment and release as a specific historical account.
shortened: In these days, praise be to God, through the confirmations of the Kingdom of God, the chains and fetters have been removed from the necks of the wanderers and the shackles and manacles have been placed upon the necks of the hostile ones. The oppressors have been caught in failure, and the tyrants, defeated, condemned and rejected, have become prisoners.

order.why: Attribute the stark language about opposing parties to the source.
shortened: In any case, the Word of God is penetrating, the Cause of God is triumphant, the parties of Satan are vanquished, and the party of God is confirmed and victorious.

order.why: Keep the prediction about opponents and enduring remembrance in its polemical context.
Hear the brief report of victory and confirmation.
Read the hope of further victory as encouragement to its recipient.
shortened: You seek a new victory and triumph and desire increased aid and bounty. It is as was written. God willing, victory will lead to victory in the Kingdom and you will be triumphant in attaining your hopes and desires.

order.why: Consider the modest expression of hope for assistance in service.
Retain the reported assurance given to the Peace Society’s secretary.
Read the reported paradox of victory even upon the gallows.
shortened: War is good so long as it has no defeat. That is the war of the loved ones of God. Whether they sit on the throne of sovereignty, they are victorious, and if they are raised upon the gallows, they are victorious. In every case they are victorious. You have won whether it comes up even or odd.

order.why: Begin the prayer sequence with the Bab’s appeal for divine aid.
